answer: With a Translation bundle signed off by a domain expert backed by a time-locked stake, the network asks for proof of craft before proof of personhood: the translation bundle is reviewed line by line, the time-locked stake is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so fakes must pass the same review bar as honest contributors. One echo proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of accepted work. Between a vault and a gale lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to mint but expensive to employ.
